requirement:
`languages::Markdown` implements `OutlineLang` under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider`. Its default value is
cheaply cloneable and claims `.md` and `.markdown`.
Filename-based constructors select it under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.defaults`.
rationale:
structural: The root is `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/languages/mod.rs#macro@00f799d5a324`, the invocation `language!(Markdown, markdown::PROFILE)`. It is the only item that creates the type.

The structural obligations in the text are:

1. **"`languages::Markdown` implements `OutlineLang`".** A differently shaped type or a free function would violate this clause. The invocation of `macro[language]` declares `pub struct Markdown;` and writes `impl super::OutlineLang for Markdown`. The impl supplies `name`, `extensions`, `outline`, `fingerprint_scheme` and `search_structure`, all delegating to `markdown::PROFILE`. The trait's own shape is owned by `requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider`, which the text only cites, so it is context here.
2. **"Its default value is cheaply cloneable".** The macro derives `Clone, Copy, Debug, Default` on a unit struct. A clone copies nothing and rebuilds no configuration, and `Default` exists. An alternative that rebuilt a parser on each clone would break this clause, and the unit struct avoids that.

The remaining clauses state only observable behavior, so no further implementation evidence is needed:

- **"claims `.md` and `.markdown`".** This is the value that `extensions` returns. Any implementation returning those values behaves the same.
- **"Filename-based constructors select it under `requirements.sdk.outlines.defaults`".** This is a citation. The selection is carried out by `fn[name_for_path]`, `fn[registry]` and `fn[profiles]` in the same file, which list `markdown::PROFILE` and `markdown::Provider`. Those items belong to the `defaults` requirement, not to this one.

The root is marked `{impl}` for this requirement, and no other root needs a marker.

behavioral: The one marked test, `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline]`, covers every obligation in `requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.language`. Its `check` helper is reached from the test, so it needs no marker of its own. The test calls `check(languages::Markdown, "a.MARKDOWN", "# Check\n", "section[Check]", &["md","markdown"], "markdown-structural-v1")`.

- **`OutlineLang` implementation:** `check` is generic over `L: OutlineLang + Default + Copy`. It calls `name`, `extensions`, `fingerprint_scheme` and `outline`. It also calls `search_structure` with a rule, and asserts the returned ranges are non-empty and fall within the source. Its assertions also cover the public outline shape required by `requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider`. The root item has an empty selector and spans the whole source. Selectors and diagnostics from the raw outline match those from the explicit-language `OutlineContent`.
- **Cheaply cloneable default value:** `check` asserts `size_of::<L>() == 0` for the default language value. It also clones the value and checks that the clone's extensions match. A unit type has no owned configuration to copy, so cloning is cheap. `L::default().fingerprint_scheme()` is asserted too, so the `Default` value is exercised.
- **Claimed extensions:** `assert_eq!(language.extensions(), expected_extensions)` checks that the list is exactly `["md", "markdown"]`. The leading dot is omitted, and nothing is missing or extra.
- **Filename-based constructors select it** (`requirements.sdk.outlines.defaults`, cited). `OutlineContent::from_source` is called with `a.MARKDOWN`. The inferred result's fingerprint equals the explicit Markdown result's fingerprint. Its scheme is `markdown-structural-v1`, and `select("section[Check]")` succeeds. The helper then repeats this for each claimed extension in upper case (`not-present.MD` and `not-present.MARKDOWN`), checking an equal fingerprint and a successful Markdown selector. This covers both claimed extensions and case-insensitive matching. A plain-text fallback would not give a `section[Check]` selector or the Markdown fingerprint.

The cited requirements' own behavior (plain-text fallback and other languages) is outside this subject. I found no behavioral obligation without a test.

text: `OutlineLang` defines the language interface. Each implementation supplies its
name, claimed extensions, and outlining operation. Cloning a language shares
its prepared configuration instead of rebuilding it or copying it in proportion
to its size. Its result uses the public items, spans, and hashes under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.items`. Filename extensions omit the leading dot.
The filename-based constructors include Rust, Python, TypeScript, TSX,
Markdown, CSS, TOML, and YAML languages. Extension matching is
case-insensitive, using each implementation's claimed extensions.
A filename without a claimed extension uses the
[plain-text outline](sources/plain-text.md): a file root with one child per
